reviews.body:
I streamed a partial snapshot (`{"f": <value>, "summary": "in prog`) through `Partial[M]` for several annotations of `f`, using `Step = Annotated[StepModel, Field(...)]`, on `main`, this branch and #3062. The table shows the type of the first nested item.

| annotation of `f` | main | this PR | #3062 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list[A]` | dict | Step | Step |
| `Optional[A]` | dict | Step | Step |
| `A \| None` | dict | Step | Step |
| `list[A] \| None` | dict | Step | Step |
| `dict[str, A]` | dict | Step | Step |
| `list[list[A]]` | dict | Step | Step |
| `Annotated[Optional[Step], ...]` | Step | Step | Step |
| `Union[A, int]` | dict | dict | dict |

The fix works. `tests/dsl/test_partial.py` gives 78 passed (77 on `main`).

**Overlap:** #3062 was opened about 4 hours earlier for the same issue (#3058). It adds the same `_strip_annotated` helper and calls it at the same four places in `_unwrap_optional_base_model` and `_build_partial_value`. The two PRs give the same result on every case above, and they will conflict. #3062's test also covers `Annotated[list[Annotated[Step, ...]], ...]` and the `Optional[Annotated[list[...]]]` variant, which this test doesn't. Maintainers will probably want to merge only one of them.

`Union[A, int]` still gives a dict on all three. I did not check whether a plain `Union[Step, int]` without `Annotated` does the same, so this may be a separate gap.

(I made this review with help from Claude Code. I ran the table above on `main`, this branch and #3062, plus `tests/dsl/test_partial.py` on each. I did not run the full test suite or a real streaming model call.)
